body.statement:
Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) be independent centered random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), let \(S=m^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^m x_j\), and let \(G\) be centered Gaussian with \(\operatorname{Cov}(G)=\operatorname{Cov}(S)\).  Suppose that constants \(b_1,b_2>0\) and \(B_m\ge1\) satisfy, for every \(j\le m\) and \(\ell\le p\),
\[
 E\exp(|x_{j\ell}|/B_m)\le2,
 \qquad
 b_1^2\le m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^mE[x_{j\ell}^2]\le b_2^2,
 \qquad
 m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^mE[x_{j\ell}^4]\le B_m^2b_2^2.
\]
Then Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike (2022), Theorem 2.1 and its equivalent hyperrectangle formulation, imply
\[
 \sup_{A\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}}
 \left|P\{S\in A\}-P\{G\in A\}\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{B_m^2\log^5(pm)}{m}\right\}^{1/4},
\]
where \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}\) is the class of axis-aligned hyperrectangles and \(C\) depends only on \(b_1,b_2\).  No positive lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of \(\operatorname{Cov}(S)\) is required.

source.locator: Theorem 2.1 and the equivalent hyperrectangle formulation in equation (15), pages 2568--2569
